The approach was adopted for projects requiring efficient ray tracing and memory savings, as regular grids consume considerable memory and require intersection tests for every voxel [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the approach (Sparse Voxel Octree) was adopted for projects requiring efficient ray tracing and memory savings, citing that regular grids consume considerable memory and require intersection tests for every voxel. Source [S1] explicitly supports this in the first passage: it mentions that regular grids (matrices) have 'considerably greater memory consumption than necessary' ('el consumo de memoria es considerablemente mayor del necesario') and are unsuitable for 'efficient Ray Tracing algorithms' because 'for each execution of the Ray Caster... an intersection test must be executed for each voxel of the model' ('para cada ejecución del Ray Caster 2 habrá que ejecutar un test de intersección por cada vóxel del modelo'). It then introduces the Octree as the structure that works for these needs. Section 3.4 also confirms that the Octree allows saving memory space ('permite ahorrar espacio en memoria'). Therefore, all facts in the claim are present in the evidence.

The algorithm expands the octree by creating a new layer of nodes above the root [S1, unofficial].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes an algorithm for growing the octree. It states that instead of pre-calculating size, the octree increases its depth/spatial extent as new voxels are processed. Specifically, the 'Growth Loop' and 'Algoritmo 1' show that for every child of the root, a new node is created, the existing child is moved to become a child of this new node, and the new node becomes the new child of the root. This process effectively creates a new layer of nodes above the previous root level (or rather, expands the root's children to accommodate deeper levels, effectively pushing the previous structure down one level in the hierarchy relative to the new root's children). The claim that the algorithm 'expands the octree by creating a new layer of nodes above the root' is a simplified but accurate description of the mechanism where the root's children are replaced by new nodes that contain the old children, thereby increasing the depth and spatial extent.
